Archival Dispatch: 26 Master Broadcasts Dated Across This I Believe (Harry S. Truman), Cecil and Sally, AFRS Basic Music Library, and Aunt Mary

Author: radio index
Reading: 5 min

Batch 46 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 46 resolves 26 landmark radio broadcasts: 8 personal philosophy broadcasts from Edward R. Murrow's acclaimed This I Believe (highlighted by former U.S. President Harry S. Truman stating his life creed, UCLA Chancellor Raymond B. Allen, Italian Renaissance art scholar Bernard Berenson, and 20th Century Limited locomotive engineer William B. Thompson), 8 sequential 1931 NBC Pacific episodes from Cecil and Sally, 8 Armed Forces Radio Service transcription discs from the AFRS Basic Music Library (featuring Sam Cooke live at the Copacabana, Louis Jordan's Tympany Five, and Bob Wills' Texas Playboys), and 2 sequential dramatic chapters from the daytime serial Aunt Mary.

1. This I Believe — 1952–1955 Edward R. Murrow CBS Radio Series

Personal philosophies of distinguished world figures and everyday citizens:

Original Circulating Filename Canonical Title Verified Airdate Speaker & Personal Creed

This_I_Believe_Raymond_Allen.mp3 "This I Believe: Dr. Raymond B. Allen (Chancellor of UCLA)" 1953-06-23 Academic freedom and spiritual foundations of higher education.
This_I_Believe_Bernard_Berenson.mp3 "This I Believe: Bernard Berenson (Art Historian & Critic)" 1955-04-12 90-year-old scholar reflects from Florence on art and human dignity.
This_I_Believe_Mario_Pei.mp3 "This I Believe: Mario Pei (Columbia University Linguist)" 1954-02-16 The power of universal language and communication in human empathy.
This_I_Believe_Clarence_Pickett.mp3 "This I Believe: Clarence E. Pickett (Nobel Peace Prize Leader, AFSC)" 1952-11-18 Quaker leader on peaceful conflict resolution and international aid.

This_I_Believe_Bennett_Schauffler.mp3 "This I Believe: Bennett F. Schauffler (NLRB Regional Director)" 1953-09-08 Labor mediator on finding common ground in industrial disputes.
